digest.en: Iran claims it hit a U.S. radar in Bahrain, escalating tensions in the Gulf. Meanwhile, Russia’s diesel tankers are finding new buyers despite U.S. pressure. The Ukraine peace talks produced little, leaving the diplomatic track stalled.
digest.hi: होर्मुज स्ट्रेट में एलपीजी टैंकर का विस्फोट और बहरीन में अमेरिकी रडार पर ईरानी हमला इस घंटे की प्रमुख घटनाएं हैं। इनके साथ ही पाकिस्तान-भारत सीमा पर कलात में बीएलए के हमले की पूरी विवरण सामने आया है।

articles.title: Did China’s ‘beauty stratagem’ find a new victim in Jensen Huang?
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after media reports revealed an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang. The Singapore-based executive is suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence. This incident has raised concerns about a potential honey trap targeting a major American tech leader. Extramarital activities have led to the resignation of one of America’s most influential tech bosses, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

articles.title: Iran says it struck U.S. military radar in Bahrain
articles.summary: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard claimed it struck a U. S. military radar in Bahrain. The group declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to traffic. The U. S. Navy countered by opening a southern route for commercial vessels while maintaining a blockade of Iranian ports. The IRGC says the strait is closed, while the U. S. Navy claims that it has opened a southern route for commercial vessels to exit and enter the critical waterway, while maintaining its “ironclad blockade” of Iranian ports.

articles.title: ‘More the bhakts comment, better it would do,’ says Rahul Gandhi on BJP’s criticisms
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi responded to BJP criticisms of his book by saying more comments would help its sales. He stated that critics are reading the work despite their objections. The remark came during an Instagram question and answer session with followers. Responding to a question during an ‘Ask Me’ session on Instagram, Rahul Gandhi said, “It is a great book, they are all reading it.

articles.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
articles.summary: Storm Charles brought heavy rain and strong winds to southern Europe. Portugal and southern Spain faced significant flooding and flight cancellations. The weather system first hit the island of Madeira before moving toward the mainland on 11 November. Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninusla this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain.

articles.title: China’s demographic challenge becoming its biotech advantage
articles.summary: The Biotechnology Innovation Organization urged Washington to adopt a national biotechnology strategy. The group warned that China is rapidly gaining ground in the sector. Biotech is now viewed as critical to economic competitiveness and national security in the U. S. Is biotechnology becoming the next space race? The Biotechnology Innovation Organization (BIO) appears to think so. This month, it urged Washington to adopt a comprehensive national biotechnology strategy, warning that China is rapidly gaining ground in an industry now viewed as critical to economic competitiveness and national security.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV denounces ‘machismo,’ demands women be protected in emotional return to Peru
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV returned to Peru, urging the Catholic hierarchy to model unity and protect women from machismo. He instructed Peruvian bishops to address clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice. The visit emphasized accountability within the local church structure. Pope Leo called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice.

articles.title: Russia's Propaganda Machine Deploys Pro-War AI Songs
articles.summary: A Ukrainian nonprofit found nearly 1,000 AI-generated songs on Russian streaming platforms. The tracks support the military and the war in Ukraine. The content aims to generate patriotic sentiment among listeners. The study highlights the scale of this digital propaganda effort. Russians using streaming music sites might find a new genre turning up in their feeds: AI-generated songs in support of Russia's military and the war in Ukraine.

articles.title: Russian Diesel Tankers Turned Away From US, But Ukraine Says Moscow Is Still Finding Buyers
articles.summary: Russian diesel tankers bound for the United States changed course after failing to find American buyers. Political and legal opposition to the Trump administration's push for Russian fuel imports blocked the deals. Ukraine reports Moscow is still securing alternative buyers for the cargoes. Several Russian diesel tankers initially bound for the United States have changed course after struggling to find American buyers willing to accept the controversial cargoes, amid mounting political and legal opposition to the Trump administration's efforts to facilitate Russian fuel imports.

articles.title: Nord Stream Gas Fueled This German Power Plant, Now It's Being Dismantled And Sent To Ukraine
articles.summary: The Greifswald power plant in northeast Germany is being dismantled and shipped to Ukraine. Built at the Nord Stream pipeline landfall, the station sat idle after the gas line was sabotaged. It joins other major European energy facilities being broken up for Ukrainian use. The Greifswald industrial power plant was built at the landfall of Russia's Nord Stream pipelines in northeast Germany.

articles.title: What Happened At The Ukraine-Russia Peace Talks? Not Much.
articles.summary: White House envoys traveled to Moscow to meet Vladimir Putin following two days of peace talks in Abu Dhabi. Russian negotiators maintained hard-line demands extending beyond the Ukraine war to the post-World War II European political structure. The talks produced no immediate breakthrough. The White House envoys fly to Moscow for meetings with Putin a day after two days of peace talks in Abu Dhabi wrapped up.

articles.title: Aid is the ‘only hope’ for millions in Sudan, WFP chief warns, as funding cuts deepen hunger crisis
articles.summary: The World Food Programme chief warned that funding cuts are deepening Sudan's hunger crisis. He visited displaced families struggling to feed their children during his first field mission. Aid remains the only viable option for millions facing starvation in the conflict zone. The World Food Programme’s (WFP) new Executive Director has warned that funding cuts are worsening Sudan’s hunger crisis following his first field mission to the country, where he met families displaced by conflict and struggling to feed their children.

articles.title: New platform aims to get money moving before disaster strikes
articles.summary: UN agencies launched a joint platform at COP31 in Antalya to secure over $3 billion in risk financing. The initiative aims to protect 75 million people from climate shocks by 2030. This move seeks to move funds before disasters strike. UN agencies on Thursday launched a joint platform at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, that aims to secure access to more than $3 billion in risk financing to protect 75 million people and their livelihoods from climate shocks and natural hazards by 2030.

articles.title: Cities rise up the climate agenda as leaders face demands for action
articles.summary: World leaders at COP31 focused on protecting cities and vulnerable communities from climate impacts. Activists simultaneously challenged governments to implement stronger action. The human cost of rising seas and melting glaciers dominated the agenda. From flooded homes to melting Himalayan glaciers, the human cost of climate change took centre stage at COP31 on Thursday, as world leaders turned their attention to protecting cities and vulnerable communities, while activists challenged governments to do more.

articles.title: More than 1,000 killed between July and September, UN report reveals
articles.summary: A UN report states over 1,000 people were killed in Haiti between July and September. Armed gangs continue to terrorize residents in Port-au-Prince and surrounding areas. The violence persists despite ongoing international concerns. More than 1,000 people were killed in Haiti during the third quarter of this year, as armed gangs continue to terrorize the population in the capital Port-au-Prince and beyond, the UN team in the island nation, said in its latest human rights report.

articles.title: Arrests, Attacks, And A Familiar Kremlin Refrain
articles.summary: US, Ukraine, and Russia held trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. Negotiations focused on broad security questions while deep gaps remained over Donbas territorial control. Russia continued military attacks on Ukraine and domestic crackdowns on citizens during the discussions. At the first US-Ukraine-Russia negotiations since February, talk turns to broad questions of security while wide gaps remain over core issues such as territorial control in the Donbas.

articles.title: Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the history of ‘sexpionage’
articles.summary: Intelligence agencies often target key individuals to compromise them. This involves damaging reputations or creating situations where sensitive information might be disclosed. Such tactics aim to gain access to data adversaries do not want shared. A large portion of intelligence work is focused on collecting information your competitor or adversary does not want you to have. But another key focus of intelligence is on compromising key individuals.

articles.title: Prabowo gains upper hand as Gibran’s exit weakens Widodo’s grip
articles.summary: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned, shifting power dynamics. President Prabowo Subianto gained the upper hand as Jokowi lost his direct presence in the administration. Jokowi had previously helped carry Prabowo to the presidency in 2024. Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka’s resignation may mark a turning point in the balance of power between President Prabowo Subianto and his predecessor, Joko Widodo.

articles.title: Argentinian lawyer mocks UK’s sovereignty claim in Falklands oil case
articles.summary: Argentina's lawyer Marcelo Kohen mocked Britain's sovereignty claims in a Hamburg tribunal hearing. He argued the UK should not act as a colonial power. Kohen rejected the historic doctrine of British maritime dominance over Falklands waters. Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceansBritain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici, Argentina has told an international tribunal. Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently belie.

articles.title: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador
articles.summary: Ecuadorian journalist Tomás Beltrán was shot dead while parking his car in Calceta. The killing highlights deteriorating security conditions in the country. Gang warfare over drug routes has made the Pacific coastline a key flashpoint. Tomás Beltrán was shot dead amid gang warfare that has turned Latin American country into one of its most violentTomás Beltrán was manoeuvring his car into his garage on Sunday night when the Ecuadorian journalist was shot dead. Beltrán ran a Facebook page with news about Calceta, a small city in the province of Manabí, whose Pacific coastline has made it a key flashpoint in the gang warfare over d.

articles.title: From Japan to Rwanda, early warnings are saving lives – but millions remain unprotected
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that early warning systems are saving lives globally. However, millions remain unprotected as warnings fail to reach them. He urged the international community to ensure every person on Earth is covered by these systems by the end of 2027. Early warning systems are saving lives across the globe, but for millions of people the warning never arrives, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Wednesday, urging the world to protect every person on Earth by the end of 2027.

articles.title: Devastation awaits returnees as UN peacekeepers prepare exit
articles.summary: UN peacekeepers are preparing to exit southern Lebanon after 48 years of patrolling the Blue Line. Hostilities have decreased following a June agreement between the United States, Lebanon, and Israel. Communities report the situation remains volatile and difficult for those attempting to rebuild their lives. The situation in southern Lebanon remains volatile and extremely difficult for communities trying to rebuild their lives, UN peacekeepers based there report, despite a significant decrease in hostilities following an agreement in June between the United States, Lebanon and Israel.

articles.title: Moscow Police Detain Hundreds Of Youths, Pressure Those Of Military Age Into Service
articles.summary: Moscow police detained hundreds of youths, including children, during a raid on an alternative gathering. Detainees reported beatings and denial of basic needs. Adults received draft notices or faced pressure to sign army contracts. Police labeled the action a preventive operation. Hundreds, including children, were detained in a raid on an alternative youth gathering in central Moscow. Detainees reported beatings and being denied water and toilets.

articles.title: IOM urges wider surveillance beyond formal routes in DR Congo
articles.summary: The International Organization for Migration urged broader surveillance beyond formal routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Seventy-one confirmed Ebola cases were detected along transit routes since the outbreak began six months ago. The agency highlighted the need to monitor movement outside standard health checkpoints. Seventy-one confirmed Ebola cases have been detected along transit routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) since the outbreak began almost six months ago, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Nearly 64,000 flee Nigeria for Niger where a humanitarian crisis is deepening
articles.summary: UNHCR reported 64,000 people fled northern Nigeria for Niger this year. Several hundred also left for Benin. Violence in the region is deepening a humanitarian crisis. Host countries are struggling to cope with the sudden influx of displaced residents. Violence in northern Nigeria is fueling a growing humanitarian crisis across the whole region: 64,000 have fled to neighbouring Niger and several hundred have left for Benin since the start of the year, as host countries struggle to cope, the UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Fact-checking site’s entire newsroom jailed as assault on press freedom widens
articles.summary: Six journalists from the Egyptian fact-checking site Matsadash remain in detention. The UN human rights office confirmed their continued imprisonment. This incident highlights a widening assault on press freedom. The government faces criticism for targeting independent media operations. Six journalists who make up the entire newsroom of the Egyptian fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention, the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said on Tuesday, warning of proliferating assaults on press freedom by the Government.

articles.title: पुतिन ने बढ़ाई डीजल सप्लाई, लेकिन अमेरिका नहीं पहुंचे टैंकर; जानें क्यों बदलना पड़ा रास्ता
articles.summary: रूस ने अक्टूबर में डीजल निर्यात दोगुना किया, पर ट्रंप-पुतिन समझौते के तहत अमेरिका के लिए भेजे गए टैंकर वहां नहीं पहुंचे। प्रतिबंधों और राजनीतिक विरोध के कारण जहाजों ने रास्ता बदला। रूस ने ब्राजील और तुर्की की ओर मुड़कर अपनी आपूर्ति पुनर्निर्देशित कर दी। वॉशिंगटन/मॉस्को। अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप और रूसी राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन के बीच डीजल आपूर्ति बढ़ाने को लेकर हुई सहमति के बाद रूस ने अक्टूबर में अपना डीजल निर्यात करीब दोगुना कर दिया।

articles.summary: होर्मुज स्ट्रेट में एलपीजी से भरा जहाज समुद्री बारूदी सुरंग से टकराया और जोरदार धमाके में तबाह हो गया। ईरान ने इस रणनीतिक जलमार्ग को बंद कर रखा है, जबकि अमेरिकी नौसेना दावा करती है कि जहाजों की आवाजाही सामान्य हो गई है। इस बावजूद कई जहाज बारूदी सुरंगों का शिकार बन रहे हैं। होर्मुज स्ट्रेट (Strait of Hormuz) में हर दिन ईरान (Iran) के आदेश का उल्लंघन करने वाले कई जहाज समुद्री बारूदी सुरंगों का शिकार बन रहे हैं।

articles.title: फिनलैंड की राजधानी हेलसिंकी में बलूच शहीद दिवस पर सेमिनार, बलूच और अफगान नेताओं ने रखे विचार
articles.summary: फिनलैंड की राजधानी हेलसिंकी में 13 नवंबर को फ्री बलूचिस्तान मूवमेंट ने बलूच राष्ट्रीय शहीद दिवस पर अंतरराष्ट्रीय सेमिनार आयोजित किया। इसमें बलूच और अफगान राष्ट्रीय आंदोलनों से जुड़े नेताओं ने हिस्सा लिया। मीर खैर बख्श मर्री की विचारधारा और स्वतंत्र बलूचिस्तान के मुद्दे पर चर्चा हुई। फिनलैंड की राजधानी हेलसिंकी में 13 नवंबर को बलूच राष्ट्रीय शहीद दिवस के मौके पर फ्री बलूचिस्तान मूवमेंट (FBM) ने अंतरराष्ट्रीय सेमिनार आयोजित किया.

articles.summary: ईरानी सेना ने बहरीन स्थित अमेरिकी रडार पर हमला किया। यह कार्रवाई अमेरिका के हालिया हमले के जवाब में हुई। ट्रंप ने चेतावनी दी थी कि अगला अमेरिकी हमला पांच गुना अधिक खतरनाक होगा। दोनों देशों के बीच शांति समझौते पर अभी सहमति नहीं बनी है। ईरान (Iran) और अमेरिका (United States of America) के बीच अभी भी शांति की स्थापना नहीं हो पाई है।

articles.summary: एलन शेपर्ड ने 6 फरवरी 1971 को चांद पर गोल्फ की दो गेंदें मारीं। यह अपोलो-14 मिशन के दौरान हुआ। उन्होंने खास क्लब तैयार करवाया था। स्पेस सूट पहनकर अभ्यास भी किया था। गोल्फ खेलने के लिए दुनिया में महंगे क्लब और शानदार मैदान हैं, लेकिन चांद पर अब तक सिर्फ एक इंसान ने यह खेल खेला है. एलन शेपर्ड ने 6 फरवरी 1971 को अपोलो-14 मिशन के दौरान चांद पर गोल्फ की दो गेंदें मारी थीं.

articles.summary: ट्रंप ने जेन्सेन हुआंग को पद छोड़ने से पहले फोन किया था। न्यूयॉर्क टाइम्स के अनुसार, ट्रंप ने उन्हें संघर्ष जारी रखने की सलाह दी। इस बातचीत की जानकारी दो सूत्रों ने दी है। अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने Nvidia के तत्कालीन CEO जेन्सेन हुआंग को पद छोड़ने से पहले फोन किया था। इस दौरान ट्रंप ने हुआंग को पद छोड़ने से पहले अपनी कुर्सी बचाने के लिए संघर्ष जारी रखने की सलाह दी थी।

articles.title: क्या दादा की संपत्ति में पोते का जन्म से होता है अधिकार? SC का बड़ा फैसला, समझें कानून
articles.summary: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने स्पष्ट किया कि दादा की मृत्यु के बाद यदि संपत्ति वारिसों में बंट चुकी हो, तो पोते का जन्म से अधिकार नहीं होता। यह फैसला हिंदू उत्तराधिकार अधिनियम, 1956 के तहत लिया गया है। दादा की संपत्ति में पोते का भी जन्म से अधिकार होता है, यह धारणा आम है. परिवारों में अक्सर यह माना जाता है कि दादा की जमीन या मकान पर बेटे के साथ-साथ पोते का भी बराबर हक होता है.

articles.title: NVIDIA के सबसे बड़े चीनी प्रतिद्वंद्वी Huawei से एलिस हुआंग का कनेक्शन, कंपनियों के जाल से
articles.summary: CNBC की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, एलिस हुआंग के पास Huawei तक Nvidia की कंप्यूटिंग पावर पहुंचाने वाली चीनी कंपनियों से संबंध हैं। यह खुलासा निजी खुफिया फर्म Tesari के दस्तावेजों के आधार पर हुआ है। Alice Huang NVIDIA Row: Nvidia के CEO जेन्सेन हुआंग के इस्तीफे के बाद इस हाई-प्रोफाइल विवाद में एक और खुलासा हुआ है। CNBC की एक रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, संदिग्ध चीनी जासूस एलिस हुआंग का संबंध उन चीनी कंपनियों से है, जिन्होंने Nvidia की कंप्यूटिंग पावर को उसके सबसे बड़े चीनी प्रतिद्वंद्वी Huawei तक पहुंचाया।
